highlights.title: Show HN: Mole – Deep research agent for your terminal
highlights.summary: Doing research with agents is fun until they blow way past budget, jumble the sources, and don't even give you the best possible answer, just sound confident. And if you want to run some research task on local data - you have no idea where your data ends up after the prompt consumes it. So I built this tool: a deep-research agent with an enforced budget, verified quotes, and a privacy boundary for local data. 1. Never spend more than you budgeted (measured overshoot is 0%). 2. Every claim carries a source 3. Data stays local (give a CSV, it'll analyze it without the data ever leaving your machine) Works with most LLMs, including coding agents, subscriptions, local models, etc. It's free and open source, would appreciate all feedback!
highlights.why: The local/open-weight ecosystem keeps making serious agent workflows cheaper to run, inspect, and iterate.

highlights.title: The Reasons Agentic Commerce Hasn't Taken Off Yet
highlights.why: Agents becoming first-class economic actors — creating accounts, buying domains, deploying code — is one of the most consequential infrastructure shifts this cycle. The agent-as-customer model changes the design space for every SaaS platform.

experimentQueue.title: Benchmark one local-first agent stack
experimentQueue.why: The local/open-weight ecosystem looks materially better this week, especially around Qwen and Forge guardrails.
experimentQueue.prompt: Pick one real workflow and compare a local Qwen+Forge stack against a frontier hosted model on tool accuracy, latency, and cost.

experimentQueue.title: Instrument one agent with better traces
experimentQueue.why: Even when state machines are not explicit, better traces are still the easiest way to understand why an agent drifted or stalled.
experimentQueue.prompt: Log tool calls, retries, and summaries for one real task, then inspect which step actually predicts success or failure.

experimentQueue.title: Stress-test one agent across model families
experimentQueue.why: The model layer is changing quickly enough that the same harness can behave very differently across providers and sizes.
experimentQueue.prompt: Replay the same agent task on one hosted frontier model and one smaller open model, then compare tool-selection behavior, not just answer quality.
